Knighthead took a minority position in January 2025, purchasing much of airline entrepreneur Maury Gallagher's stake, a move that left Johnson as the majority owner.

articles.snippet:
Amentum Services received two Army aviation-maintenance modifications totaling approximately $38.3 million and was selected for two major multiple-award contract vehicles.

articles.text:
Amentum Receives $38.3 Million In Aviation Awards And Positions On Two Major Contract Vehicles
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 4:23 PM
Amentum Receives $38.3 Million In Aviation Awards And Positions On Two Major Contract Vehicles
Amentum Services received two Army aviation-maintenance modifications totaling approximately $38.3 million and was selected for two major multiple-award contract vehicles.
The Army awarded an $18.4 million time-and-materials modification for worldwide aviation maintenance. The work includes level-of-effort support, pass-back maintenance, and aircraft modification installations.
Global Aviation Maintenance
The $18.4 million modification increased the cumulative value of contract W58RGZ-25-C-0003 to approximately $435.2 million. The full modification value was obligated using fiscal 2027 Army aircraft-procurement and operations-and-maintenance funding.
Amentum also received a $19.9 million modification under contract W58RGZ-25-C-0004. Work will be conducted at locations across Alaska, Arizona, California, Hawaii, Kansas, Montana, New Mexico, South Korea, Texas, and Washington through November 2027. The Army obligated the full amount.
These two modifications represent approximately $38.3 million in newly awarded, directly attributable value. The cumulative values of the underlying contracts are not added to that total because they include earlier awards.
Amentum was also selected for the Navy’s $7.13 billion Surface Electronic Warfare Improvement Program vehicle and the Air Force’s $16.1 billion Advanced Propulsion Enterprise contract. Those ceilings are shared with numerous companies and do not guarantee Amentum a specific amount. Actual value will depend on task orders competed and awarded under each vehicle.

articles.title: University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive
articles.snippet:
The University of Michigan Library has received a bequest of more than $21 million from Daniel T. Longone to support the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive.
The post University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 3:40 PM
University Of Michigan Library Receives More Than $21 Million For Culinary Archive
The University of Michigan Library has received a bequest of more than $21 million from Daniel T. Longone to support the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive.
The gift is the largest in the library’s history and honors Longone’s wife, Janice B. Longone, whose collecting and research helped establish the archive.
Preserving American Culinary History
The collection contains more than 30,000 cookbooks, recipes, restaurant menus, advertisements, and other materials documenting the history of food and drink in the United States.
Its holdings span the 18th through early 21st centuries, with particular strengths in community cookbooks, African American and immigrant cookbooks, handwritten recipes, restaurant menus, food advertising, wine, and viticulture.
One of its most significant items is the only known copy of Malinda Russell’s 1866 work, “A Domestic Cook Book,” the oldest known cookbook written by an African American woman.
Current collecting priorities include Native American cookbooks, regional cooking, immigrant foodways, vegetarian and vegan cuisine, and handwritten recipe collections.
Expanding Research And Public Access
The bequest will support preservation, acquisitions, cataloging, conservation, teaching, research, digitization, and public programming.
Funding will also support visiting scholars, research fellows, artists, seminars, workshops, curated digital collections, and an annual public lecture.
Longone previously contributed another $1.5 million to establish the Janice B. Longone Librarian for Culinary History. Juli McLoone, the archive’s longtime curator, holds the endowed position.
The library also plans to expand classroom access as students use the collection to investigate migration, identity, race, gender, labor, business, environmental issues, and everyday life.
KEY QUOTES:
This gift is an extraordinary investment in the future of an amazing culinary archive. The endowed librarian position provides dedicated leadership, and this level of support gives that leader the resources to preserve and build the collection, welcome and engage researchers and students, and connect its stories with the broader public. Together, these commitments ensure that Jan and Dan Longone’s vision will continue to flourish and impact scholars well into the future.
Lisa Carter, University Librarian And Dean Of Libraries At The University Of Michigan
She knew the value of looking at cookbooks unmitigated by a historian’s perspective.
Ruth Reichl, Chef And Food Writer
She would lead you down the rickety back stairs to her basement with all these dehumidifiers going and these metal racks full of books and you could spend as long as you wanted there. I thought I had struck gold.
Rick Bayless, Chef And Restaurateur

Flipper One Raises $15 Million on Kickstarter
The pocket-sized Linux mini-computer has drawn more than 27,000 pledges since its Kickstarter campaign launched.
Updated on Nov. 21, 2026 in Consumer Electronics
Kickstarter backers have pledged $15 million to the Flipper One, a pocket-sized Linux mini-computer that works with Wi-Fi and 5G networks. AI Illustration. Upload story photo >
Live Poll
Do you trust that gadgets like this won't put your home network at risk?
▲ Yes ▼ No
The Flipper One, a pocket-sized mini-computer, has raised $15 million on Kickstarter, with $13 million coming in on the first day of the campaign. The device runs Linux and uses Wi-Fi and 5G rather than the RFID and NFC protocols of its predecessor, the Flipper Zero.
Why it matters
The campaign's rapid funding signals strong interest in a portable device aimed at networks, routers, and internet-connected hardware rather than only low-level wireless signals. Its focus on regular software and cellular connectivity distinguishes it from the earlier Flipper Zero, launched in 2020.
The Flipper One runs Linux, connects over Wi-Fi and 5G, supports eSIM for cellular networks, and can act as both a Wi-Fi client and hotspot. Its raw specifications such as processor and storage were not included in the reporting.
The players
Flipper Devices
Flipper Devices is the company behind the Flipper Zero and the Flipper One, known for pocket-sized hardware tools aimed at hobbyists and security researchers.
The details
The device is designed to interact with Wi-Fi networks, routers, and internet-connected devices, and once developers gain access, additional functionality is expected to emerge. Unlike the Flipper Zero, which works with Bluetooth, RFID, and NFC, the Flipper One relies on regular software and modern cellular technologies.
Timeline
2020: The predecessor Flipper Zero was launched.
November 21, 2026: Coverage of the Flipper One Kickstarter campaign was published.
The Tech Race
The Flipper One marks a departure from the Flipper Zero's focus on raw wireless protocols, moving toward general-purpose Linux computing and network-level tools. Its design reflects a broader trend of pocket hardware that bridges hobbyist experimentation and mainstream internet connectivity.
The device could give users a portable tool for working with Wi-Fi networks, routers, and cellular connections through regular Linux software. Backers and future buyers will be able to test network-connected devices without carrying a full laptop.
The takeaway
Portable hardware that runs standard software can open network experimentation to a wider audience than specialized single-purpose tools. Readers interested in the device should watch for developer documentation as access expands.

articles.text:

Eight by Zero targets insurance data integration costs

Munich Re Life US joins as reinsurance partner
Platform connects employee data across insurance products
Eight by Zero Technologies (8/0), a Montreal-based insurance technology company developing interoperability infrastructure, has raised $3 mn in seed funding to expand its data connectivity platform across the insurance industry.
The financing round was led by Diagram, with participation from Canada Life as a strategic investor.
Eight by Zero is also working with Munich Re Life US, a subsidiary of Munich Re Group, to address employee data integration challenges affecting group insurance and disability carriers.
Insurtech Eight by Zero has secured $3 mn in seed financing led by Diagram, with strategic participation from Canada Life.
The company’s interoperability platform connects insurers, third-party administrators, employers and HR systems, reducing the need for separately maintained data integrations.
Munich Re Life US is working with Eight by Zero to address employee data connectivity challenges for group and disability insurers, while the funding will support product development and expansion.
The new capital will support product development, expansion into additional insurance lines, customer implementation capacity and commercial growth.
Eight by Zero targets insurance data integration costs
Eight by Zero has developed a multi-tenant platform that connects insurers, third-party administrators (TPAs), employers and human resources systems through APIs and file-based integrations.
The technology replaces separate point-to-point connections with a shared connectivity layer designed to reduce repetitive integration work.
Insurance carriers frequently establish individual connections with employers to obtain employee information needed for underwriting, policy administration and claims-related processes. When several insurers provide different forms of coverage to the same employer, each may need to build and maintain its own integration.
Eight by Zero aims to eliminate that duplication by establishing a connection that can serve multiple insurance products and carriers.
Carriers have rebuilt the same integration for every employer they onboard. We build it once, and the carrier can get it for every line it writes for that employer. Disability and absence are where we’re proving it. The same employee data drives every other line of coverage, and that’s where we’re headed.
Sam Kasle, Co-Founder and CEO of Eight by Zero
The platform is already used by multiple insurance carriers across North America. Artificial intelligence supports initial integration setup and ongoing maintenance, while the underlying data mapping remains deterministic.
Canada Life invests in insurance interoperability platform
Canada Life participated in the seed round as a strategic investor, supporting Eight by Zero’s development of infrastructure intended to simplify information exchange between employers and insurance providers.
Julia McGillis, Executive Vice President, Workplace Benefits & Retirement at Canada Life, said the investment aligns with the insurer’s efforts to improve connectivity across benefits and insurance services.

articles.text:
Telekom , Pours
Deutsche Telekom Pours Another Quarter-Billion Into Munich AI Site, Lands microagi as Tenant
Published on 11/22/2026 at 10:30 | Editorial boerse-global.de
Telekom plans to raise Munich AI factory capacity to 20 MW with under EUR 250 million more investment; microagi to train robotics models there.
Telekom, Pours, Another, Quarter-Billion, Into, Munich, Site, Lands, Tenant, EUR Illustration mit AI erstellt.
Deutsche Telekom is turning its Munich AI factory into a magnet for industrial robotics work while deepening its ties to the continent's most closely watched AI startup. The Bonn-based carrier said on 18 November that microagi will train its robotics models for industrial clients at the Munich site, keeping production data and manufacturing know-how in Germany and under the customers' own control.
The arrangement comes alongside a capacity upgrade: Telekom plans to lift the Munich facility's output to 20 megawatts, backed by just under a further EUR 250 million of investment. Additional NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra systems will form part of the expansion. The company is also weighing whether to extend its footprint in Bavaria beyond the announced buildout, though any such move remains subject to a final investment decision.
Sovereign AI Push Tied to Mistral Stake
Alongside the infrastructure work, Telekom is pursuing a strategic partnership with Mistral AI aimed at supplying German companies and public authorities with sovereign AI solutions. The first step in that tie-up is a EUR 100 million investment in Mistral AI by T.Capital Tech Fund, the group's venture arm, made as part of the startup's Series D financing round.
Should investors sell immediately? Or is it worth buying Deutsche Telekom?
Separately, the group disclosed on 16 November that it had repurchased roughly 4.24 million of its own shares between 9 and 13 November. Since the current buyback programme began on 10 August, it had acquired around 53.6 million treasury shares by the end of that window.
Analysts Split on Valuation
Research houses are pulling in different directions on the stock. Barclays raised its price target to EUR 33 from EUR 32 on 11 November while reaffirming its "Overweight" rating. Kepler Cheuvreux moved the other way on 18 November, cutting its target to EUR 30 from EUR 32 and keeping a "Hold" stance. The shares added 0.5% on Friday to close at EUR 26.18.

articles.title: each::labs closes seven million seed round and accelerates its generative platform
articles.snippet: each::labs closes seven million seed round and accelerates its generative platform Foro3D
articles.text:
The startup each::labs, founded in June 2024 by Turkish engineers and headquartered in San Francisco, has closed a $7 million seed round led by Revo Capital and the EBRD. Its AI image, video, and audio generation platform reached $2 million in monthly revenue in October, quintupling its billing since August, and runs nearly one million generations per day for more than 750 organizations.
Illustrative image generated with AI
Proprietary models and each::studio for audiovisual workflows 🎬
The capital will be allocated to expanding the portfolio of proprietary models such as Flint Image and Lockstep, and to developing each::studio, a tool aimed at film and VFX teams that allows working with generative media without API integration. For professionals in the sector, this represents a more controlled and reusable AI generation pathway, with specialized models that reduce the cost of failed iterations and accelerate the creation of character and motion variants in audiovisual production.
One million generations a day and there are still those asking the render to hurry up ⏱️
Nearly one million daily generations for 750 organizations sounds like someone on the VFX team will no longer have an excuse to deliver the storyboard on Monday. That said, with each::studio promising to work without touching an API, more than one technician will discover that their new most in-demand skill will be explaining to the producer that the generate button doesn't make coffee.

Telangana tech startups raise $726 mn in 9M 2026; funding rounds dip 30%: Tracxn
According to Tracxn’s analysis, most of the fresh capital flowed into a handful of large early-stage funding rounds, led by data centre company CtrlS, as well as enterprise infrastructure businesses based in Hyderabad.

Telangana-based tech companies raised $726 million in funding during the first nine months of 2026 (9M 2026), marking a 266 per cent increase from $199 million in the year-ago period and a 12 per cent rise from $647 million in 9M 2024, according to a Tracxn report.
However, the number of funding rounds declined 30 per cent to 73 from 105 a year earlier, according to the Telangana Tech – 9M 2026 Report by Tracxn, which tracks funding, investors, exits, unicorns and city-level activity between January 1 and September 30, 2026.
Advt
According to the report, most of the fresh capital flowed into a handful of large early-stage funding rounds, led by data centre company CtrlS , as well as enterprise infrastructure businesses based in Hyderabad.
However, deal activity declined, with both seed- and early-stage funding rounds falling from the year-ago period. Exit activity remained limited, while the period saw the emergence of one new unicorn, space launch company Skyroot Aerospace .
Top 10 deals drive funding
The ten largest funding rounds raised $664 million, accounting for 91 per cent of Telangana's total funding of $726 million in 9M 2026. Hyderabad-based data centre company CtrlS led the list with a $423 million Series B round in June, backed by CPP Investments.
The deal alone accounted for 58 per cent of total funding and 80 per cent of the $527 million increase over 9M 2025.
CtrlS also raised $28.2 million in a Series A round in February, taking its total funding during the period to $451 million.
Skyroot Aerospace raised $60 million in a Series C round in May, while Edubuk secured $50 million in a Series B round in March. Despite the increase in capital raised, Series A and later-stage rounds declined 18 per cent to 23 from 28. The number of first-time funded companies also fell 31 per cent to 20 from 29.
Early-stage funding surged 334 per cent to $622 million from $143 million in 9M 2025, accounting for 86 per cent of the total, said the report.
Advt
The CtrlS Series B round alone contributed 68 per cent of early-stage funding. However, the number of early-stage rounds declined 27 per cent to 19.
According to Trcxn, late-stage funding rose 426 per cent to $78.1 million from $14.8 million, across four rounds compared with two in the year-ago period. However, it remained 84 per cent below the $482 million recorded in 9M 2024. Seed-stage funding declined 35 per cent to $26.4 million, accounting for 4 per cent of the total, while seed-stage rounds fell 35 per cent to 50.
Investor participation also weakened, with the number of active investors declining 22 per cent to 61 from 78. International investors fell 43 per cent to 13 from 23, while first-time investors declined 36 per cent to 30 from 47.
